description: EXAMPLE synthetic customer personas for capsule portfolio validation. Copy to persona-panel.json and replace with personas matched to YOUR products.

personas.name: Jordan Reyes

demographics.income: $95K — day job plus ~$800/month from a side SaaS

goals: Grow the side SaaS to full-time income within two years
Automate support and marketing so nights stay free for building
Validate new feature ideas before writing any code
frustrations: Tools that require a sales call before showing pricing
Analytics dashboards that need a data team to interpret
Losing weekends to infrastructure instead of product
Newsletters and courses that repackage obvious advice
values: Ship small and iterate over polishing in private
Own the stack — export everything, no lock-in
Evidence over opinions when prioritizing features
psychographics.buyingBehavior: Discovers tools on Hacker News, IndieHackers, and developer Discords. Signs up for free tiers immediately, upgrades within a week if the tool sticks. Cancels ruthlessly at renewal if usage dropped. Prefers monthly billing until a tool proves itself for a full quarter.

willingnessToPay.course_or_content: $0-$50 (only from builders with public track records)

validationQuestions: Can Jordan get to first value in a single evening session without reading docs?
Does this replace an existing line item in Jordan's tool budget, or add a new one?
Would Jordan still pay for this in a month where the side SaaS made $0?

personas.name: Priya Nathan

goals: Cut the hours spent on repetitive client reporting each month
Standardize processes so new hires ramp in days, not months
Look competent to the agency owner by finding tools that save money
Avoid anything that requires involving the (outsourced) IT contractor
frustrations: Software that requires admin setup she is not authorized to do
Per-seat pricing that punishes adding junior staff
Migrations — she has been burned by two CRM switches
Vendors that go quiet after the sale
values: Reliability over novelty — boring tools that just work
Clear documentation and responsive human support
Predictable pricing she can defend in a budget meeting
Vendor stability — will the company exist in three years?
psychographics.buyingBehavior: Researches via G2 reviews, peer recommendations in ops communities, and vendor comparison pages. Builds a shortlist of three, trials the top pick with one client account, then writes a one-page recommendation for the business owner. Buys annual plans for the discount once trust is established.

validationQuestions: Can Priya trial this on one client account without a company-wide rollout?
Does the pricing page give her a number she can put in a budget email today?
If the tool disappeared in six months, how painful is the migration out?
